question.problem: A pump moves $\frac{9}{10}$ gallons of water in three minutes. Find the unit rate of gallons per minute.
question.worked_solution:
To compute the unit rate of gallons per minute, we divide the number of gallons, $\frac{9}{10},$ by the number of minutes, $3$, as follows:   

$$
\frac{9}{10}÷3
$$

Dividing a fraction by a whole number is equivalent to multiplying the fraction by the reciprocal of that whole number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{10}÷3 & =\frac{9}{10}÷\frac{3}{1} \\  & =\frac{9}{10}\times \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{9\times 1}{10\times 3} \\  & =\frac{3\times 3}{10\times 3} \\  & =\frac{3\times \cancel{3}}{10\times \cancel{3}} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit rate in this situation is $\frac{3}{10}$ gallons per minute.
